ge_college.note: The institution-wide Collegiate Requirements are the applicable General Education layer. Randolph-Macon publishes no separate school or subcollege requirement layer for Computer Science.

upper_division.reason: The current catalog publishes no aggregate university-wide upper-division-credit minimum. It defines courses numbered 300-399 as upper-level and courses numbered 400-499 as advanced-level. Within the Computer Science major, required CSCI 311 contributes three upper-level credits, the Programming Emphasis contributes three, and at least two three-credit electives must be numbered 300 or above, guaranteeing at least 12 major credits at that level.

residency.rule: No more than 75 combined transfer and external semester hours may apply to the 120-hour degree, yielding a 45-hour institutional-credit floor by arithmetic. At least one-half of the coursework required for the major must be completed at Randolph-Macon.

canonical_path.note: The 80-hour capacity is the arithmetic remainder after the fixed 40-hour major. It contains the nonadditive Collegiate Requirements and any remaining applicable credit; it is not a catalog-published General Education subtotal.

modeling_notes: This composition selects the current ordinary Computer Science major designated for the Bachelor of Science and excludes the separately published Cybersecurity and Data Science programs.

The live 2026-2027 major is modeled exactly as seven Foundation courses totaling 25 hours, one three-hour Programming Emphasis choice, and four additional three-hour electives, at least two numbered 300 or above, for 40 hours.

The catalog does not publish one independent Collegiate Requirements credit subtotal. Effective Communication courses, Pillars, Cross-Area attributes, major overlap, and the zero-credit Physical Education and Wellness experiences therefore remain explicit completion gates inside the 80-hour post-major capacity rather than being gross-summed.
The 45-hour institutional-credit floor is derived from the official 120-hour degree minimum and 75-hour combined transfer/external-credit maximum; it is not separately worded as a residence minimum.

The current target is a student entering Fall 2026 or later. The 120-hour minimum began with Fall 2023 entrants, and the two no-credit Physical Education and Wellness experiences apply to Fall 2026 entrants and later.

The degree-summary page still mentions two 100-level physical-education courses while its detailed current rule and footnote define two approved no-credit experiences for Fall 2026 entrants and later. The detailed cohort-specific rule is modeled, and the wording conflict remains flagged.

The evaluator must enforce four distinct major electives, at least two numbered 300 or above, without reusing the selected Programming Emphasis course.
The 45-hour institutional floor is arithmetic derived from the 75-hour external-credit cap, not separately phrased as a residence minimum.
The degree-summary bullet retains 100-level-course wording, while the detailed current rule and cohort footnote require two approved no-credit experiences for Fall 2026 entrants and later.
